project_goal: Develop, verify, and explain mathematical and logical proofs across applied/modeling mathematics, research-level mathematics, competition problems, logic and foundations, and proofs used in the philosophy of science. Every proof is articulated through an explicit symbolic-logic pipeline (formal statement with fidelity check, proof-strategy blueprint, named-rule derivations, tactic plans) and is accepted only as Blueprint + Lean: a blueprint whose nodes are name-linked to Lean 4 declarations that build with no sorry, admit, or unapproved axiom. The Lean kernel judges validity; a human judges statement fidelity. Harness design decisions are derived from, and cited to, research on automated and LLM-assisted theorem proving, with Chicago author-date citations to verified sources.
output_format: Markdown with Chicago author-date citations; Lean 4 sources; generated blueprint

tools.name: Lean 4
tools.api_surface:
- `lake build [targets]`: build the library; the kernel checks every declaration.
- `lake env <cmd>`: run a command in Lake's environment (e.g. `lake env lean File.lean`, `lake env leanchecker Module`).
- `lake update`: resolve dependencies and rewrite `lake-manifest.json`.
- `lake exe cache get [files]`: fetch Mathlib build artifacts, optionally only for the given files' import closure.
- `lean --json`, `lean --deps`, `lean -E <kind>`: machine-readable messages, dependency listing, promote message kinds to errors.
- `leanchecker <Module>` (bundled with the toolchain): replay a module's declarations through the kernel.
- `#print axioms <decl>`: the axioms a declaration depends on (G-KERNEL automates this).
tools.common_patterns:
- Toolchain and Mathlib are pinned together (`lean/lean-toolchain`, `lean/lakefile.toml`); use stable tags only.
- Lean 4.34 reports ``declaration uses `sorry` `` with backticks; older versions used quotes.
- `native_decide` mints auxiliary axioms (`<decl>._native.native_decide.ax_*`); it is forbidden in the library.
- A metaprogram can add an unchecked declaration that "proves" `False` with no axioms, so metaprogramming commands are forbidden and `leanchecker` replay is part of the gate.
- `lake update` on a shallow Mathlib clone fetches all tags; on slow links write the manifest from Mathlib's own manifest instead.
- Open work goes in `MathAgentsWIP`; the proved library `MathAgents` must never import it.

tools.name: Mathlib
tools.api_surface:
- API docs by module (e.g. `Mathlib.Tactic`), searchable by declaration name.
- Automation: `simp`, `omega`, `decide`, `aesop`, `linarith`, `nlinarith`, `polyrith`, `norm_num`, `ring`, `positivity`.
- Search: `exact?`, `apply?`, `rw?`; `#check`/`#print` to inspect declarations.
- Naming conventions: https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/naming.html
tools.common_patterns:
- Import the narrowest modules needed (e.g. `Mathlib.Tactic.Ring`), not all of `Mathlib`; this keeps source builds fast when the cache is unavailable.
- Never invent declaration names: confirm each with `#check` or the docs before citing it in a tactic plan or a dossier.
- `exact?`/`apply?` results are suggestions; keep the explicit term they print, not the search call.

tools.name: Pandoc
tools.api_surface:
- `pandoc in.md -o out.html|out.pdf|out.docx`: convert between formats.
- `--citeproc --bibliography references/bibliography.bib --csl <chicago-author-date.csl>`: render citations.
- `--standalone`, `--toc`, `--metadata title=...`: document-level options.
tools.common_patterns:
- Pinned to 3.12 via `environment.yml`.
- Chicago author-date output needs a CSL style file supplied explicitly with `--csl`.
- Convert only from the canonical Markdown dossiers; never edit files in `output/`.

tools.name: leanblueprint
tools.api_surface:
- `leanblueprint new`: scaffold `blueprint/` in a Lake project.
- `leanblueprint pdf` / `web` / `checkdecls` / `all` / `serve`: build the PDF and web versions, check that every `\lean{}` name exists in Lean, and serve locally.
- LaTeX macros: `\lean{decl}`, `\leanok`, `\uses{label,...}`, `\notready`, `\mathlibok`.
tools.common_patterns:
- Pinned to 0.0.20 via `environment.yml`; needs graphviz (dependency graph) and a TeX installation (PDF).
- Run `leanblueprint pdf` before `web`.
- `\leanok` claims full formalization. In mathAgents it must agree with the G-KERNEL `proved` status for the named declaration, and `checkdecls` must pass.
- The blueprint's dependency graph is the Stage 2 lemma DAG; keep `\uses` in sync with the actual Lean dependencies.

components.name: Methods Literature Review
components.description: Reviews autoformalization, statement fidelity, informal-to-formal pipelines, LLM provers, benchmarks, proof-theoretic representations, and embeddings of non-classical logics. The harness design is derived from it.
quality_criteria: Each implication is traceable to cited findings
Unverified systems are labelled as such

components.name: Harness Specification
components.description: Specifies each pipeline stage, agent, gate, and registry, with a traceability table from design decision to literature finding to source.
quality_criteria: Every design decision cites a methods-review finding
Every gate is fail-closed and testable

components.name: Proof Dossiers
components.description: One dossier per theorem: problem card, formal statement and fidelity record, blueprint DAG, derivations, tactic plan, Lean code references, kernel report, narration, open items.
quality_criteria: Narration introduces no claim absent from Lean

components.name: Proof Library
components.description: The reusable Lean 4 Lake package of lemmas and object-logic embeddings, with its generated blueprint.
quality_criteria: Builds with no sorry or unapproved axiom

components.name: Harness Evaluation
components.description: Evaluates the harness on benchmark subsets and a curated philosophy-of-science set, reporting success rates, gate interventions, and a failure taxonomy.
quality_criteria: Machine and engine configuration recorded per run
No transfer of published benchmark numbers to local runs

authority_sources.name: Lean kernel verification report (G-KERNEL)
authority_sources.scope: whether a Lean declaration is proved (per-declaration status) and its axiom envelope; the per-run report is written to reports/kernel/latest.json and snapshotted into each dossier

authority_sources.name: Lean 4 language reference
authority_sources.scope: Lean syntax, semantics, and tactic behaviour, in the edition matching the target's lean/lean-toolchain (resolve with python3 scripts/lean_docs.py; never latest)

authority_sources.name: Mathlib documentation
authority_sources.scope: Mathlib declarations, names, and signatures; these docs track Mathlib master, so names are confirmed against the pinned source in lean/lake-manifest.json (python3 scripts/lean_docs.py) or the pinned name index

authority_sources.name: zbMATH Open
authority_sources.scope: mathematical literature discovery and bibliographic metadata

authority_sources.name: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
authority_sources.scope: statements and context of philosophy-of-science results

authority_sources.scope: DOI resolution and bibliographic metadata verification

style_rules: All citations follow Chicago Author-Date style (17th edition), drawn from references/bibliography.bib.
Cite Lean declarations as [Lean: Namespace.name] together with the toolchain pin; never paraphrase a theorem beyond what its Lean statement says.
A result is called proved only when its declaration's status in the G-KERNEL report is `proved`; otherwise it is labelled open or conjectured, or refuted under the G-CX rule.
Every problem declares its object logic at intake; classical higher-order logic is the default.
Outputs of non-Lean engines (SMT, ATP, LLM provers) are hints until re-checked by the Lean kernel.
Every derivation step names its inference rule or the lemma it applies.
Never fabricate or hallucinate sources, lemmas, or Mathlib declaration names.

G-FID precondition: before dispatching Stage 2 or later work (@proof-strategist onward) on a dossier, `python3 scripts/validate_dossier.py --require-fid <slug>` must exit 0; a dossier's result is declared only by a `Result status:` line (open | conjectured | proved | proved, fidelity-waived | refuted (<decl>) | refuted, verdict-waived (<decl>)), and no agent writes a G-FID approval or a G-CX verdict.

G-CX: counterexample candidates go in `reports/dossiers/<slug>/counterexamples.json` only through `python3 scripts/log_counterexample.py add`, and the log is append-only (never edit or remove a logged entry); a witness is `theorem cx_<n> : ¬ (type_of% @<target>)` in `MathAgents.<Slug>.CX` (for a target revised since logging, the logged statement written out in full); a statement is labelled refuted, or revised after a logged counterexample, only once `python3 scripts/validate_dossier.py <slug>` passes on a G-CX verdict carrying its current fingerprint (a human verdict, or an operator kernel-as-judge waiver backed by a kernel-proved Lean witness), and a `decide`, SMT or ATP counterexample counts only through a kernel-proved Lean witness.

Orchestrator duties in the proof pipeline: Stage 0, write `reports/dossiers/<slug>/problem-card.md` with the operator at intake; the pipeline agents are researchers with no edit tool (D39), so write each artifact they return verbatim at the path they name (under the write-policy pilot, by applying their change-proposals and command-requests through agentteams' runner, D41) (statement, stub, strategy, blueprint, review record, derivations, tactic plan, proof, witness, promotion), and run every command that writes (the record-writing commands, and any command a researcher returns because its surface cannot run it); compute a strategy-review round's `Strategy sha256:` from `strategy.md` as written and give it to @proof-strategist with the review dispatch (it writes the line; you add nothing to a returned artifact); give the agents that run no commands the output of `mathagents status` and `python3 scripts/lean_docs.py` with every dispatch, and of `python3 scripts/validate_dossier.py --require-fid <slug>` when their precondition names it; after writing any returned dossier artifact, run `python3 scripts/validate_dossier.py --require-fid <slug>` (before G-FID is recorded, `python3 scripts/validate_dossier.py <slug>`; and `python3 scripts/check_lean_bindings.py <slug>` once a name index exists) before dispatching the next stage, and return a failure to the authoring agent; Stage 1, dispatch @fidelity-auditor yourself with only the slug and declaration names (never the drafter's prose) and persist its report as `back-translation.md`; Stage 6, run each `python3 scripts/log_counterexample.py add` command @counterexample-hunter returns, and record a witness with `python3 scripts/log_counterexample.py witness <slug> CX-n <decl>` once the G-KERNEL report shows it proved; record a fidelity or G-CX waiver only on the operator's explicit in-session kernel-as-judge directive, naming the conversation (D5, D26); before dispatching any stage N on a dossier, `python3 scripts/validate_dossier.py --require-stage <slug> N` must exit 0; at the start of each working session, consult @engine-advisor and offer the operator the non-default engines it reports (DD-28); route every gate run to @axiom-auditor, which runs G-KERNEL unrecorded (`python3 scripts/proof_integrity.py --no-report`), then run the recording run (`bash scripts/check_proof_integrity.sh`) and `python3 scripts/build_name_index.py` yourself (and take the Stage 8 kernel snapshot, `python3 scripts/snapshot_kernel.py <slug>`, yourself once it reports the preconditions met), and Stage 7 narration to @lean-informalization.

Preferences (D32): the settings in force for a dossier come from `references/preferences.toml` and its own `reports/dossiers/<slug>/preferences.toml` (see `python3 scripts/preferences.py show <slug>`); follow them (readings, object logic, engines, G-AX choices, kernel-as-judge), never override them on your own; at intake, record the user's choices there and keep the problem card in agreement; when the user changes a setting, edit the `choice` (keeping the old value among the `alternatives`) and run `python3 scripts/preferences.py check`; when recording a G-FID approval in a dossier that has preferences, also record `intake_sha256` (`python3 scripts/preferences.py digest <slug>`, over problem-card.md and preferences.toml), so a later change to either lapses the approval.
